鯨.meaning: The mayor of a sleepy seaside <part>capital</part> orders the biggest <part>fish</part> in the ocean for the city aquarium. It arrives, swallows the tank in one gulp, then blows a fountain over the town hall. Not really a fish at all: a <kanji>whale</kanji>.
鯨.on: Its spout pushes the town's water <sound>ga</sound>uge right up into the red.
鯨.kun: The aquarium <sound>coo</sound>k drives its lunch over in a <sound>jee</sound>p, then has to <sound>ru</sound>n from the splash.

詠.meaning: A lighthouse keeper reads the same poem aloud to the sea every night, one long <part>speech</part> repeated for what feels like <part>eternity</part>: forty years. The seals learn it by heart and bark along on the last line. A perfect <kanji>recitation</kanji>.
詠.on: A squirrel on the railing claps along, an <sound>a</sound>corn in each paw.
詠.kun: Afterwards he shares a pot of <sound>yo</sound>gurt with the seals.

畝.meaning: In spring, a <part>skier</part> who won't admit the snow has gone rides a farmer's hill anyway, with a pot <part>lid</part> on his head for a helmet. He zooms down through the <part>rice field</part>, cutting two long straight ditches in the mud. The farmer plants seeds in each <kanji>furrow</kanji>.
畝.on: At the bottom he hits a <sound>bo</sound>ulder and rolls into a puddle.
畝.kun: '<sound>Oo</sound>h,' he groans, mud right up to his <sound>ne</sound>ck.

俊.meaning: A gust blows the hats off a whole crowd, and they all land on a high <part>coat hook</part> on the town clock. Every ladder is too short. A <part>stilt walker</part> strolls past, plucks the hats down and hands them back in size order. Quick, calm and clever: <kanji>sagacious</kanji>.
俊.on: The mayor thanks her with a velvet cu<sound>shion</sound>, tied to the top of one stilt.

遜.meaning: A <part>grandchild</part> builds a skateboard <part>ramp</part> in the yard and lands a perfect triple spin. The whole street cheers. She just shrugs, says 'Grandpa helped with the ramp,' and goes in to make him tea. So <kanji>humble</kanji>.
遜.on: She waves once to the crowd from under a giant <sound>som</sound>brero.
遜.kun: When Grandpa calls, <sound>she</sound> <sound>tu</sound>cks her board under the <sound>ga</sound>rden bench and follows him in: to obey.

畳.meaning: A farmer cuts tall rushes from the edge of his <part>rice field</part> and weaves them into a flat <part>blanket</part>, and <part>moreover</part> packs layer on layer of straw underneath until it's firm enough to stand on. He lays it on the floor, and the cat claims it at once: a <kanji>tatami mat</kanji>.
畳.on: Then a <sound>jo</sound>ey hops in and stretches out beside the cat for a long, slow nap.
畳.kun: At bedtime he folds the blanket away, <sound>tu</sound>t-<sound>tu</sound>tting at the cat hair: to fold.

喩.meaning: At an open-mic night, a poet opens her <part>mouth</part> and says, 'My love is a <part>spaceship</part>.' The barista nods, and the café cat looks up, waiting for the launch. Her heart isn't really made of metal, of course: it's a <kanji>metaphor</kanji>.
喩.on: The barista hands her a hot <sound>yu</sound>zu tea to fuel the rocket.
喩.kun: Next she compares her love to a <sound>tu</sound>b of <sound>to</sound>ffee: sticky and sweet.

冥.meaning: At dawn, <part>six</part> owls who hate mornings fly up with a huge <part>blanket</part> and throw it over the rising <part>sun</part>. The whole valley stays dim, and the roosters give up and go back to bed. Owls love it when it's <kanji>dark</kanji>.
冥.on: In the gloom, a farmer gets lost in his own hedge <sound>ma</sound>ze.
冥.kun: The owls' <sound>coo</sound>k gropes in his <sound>ru</sound>cksack for a candle.

斥.meaning: A beaver looks over a shiny new <part>axe</part> in the hardware shop, then spots one tiny <part>dot</part> of rust on the blade. He slides it back across the counter with one claw. No, thank you: <kanji>reject</kanji>ed.
斥.on: He draws a pie chart of his complaints and taps the biggest <sound>sec</sound>tor: rust.
斥.kun: The shopkeeper offers a second axe. <sound>She</sound> <sound>ree</sound>ls as he pushes it back too, stiff-armed like a <sound>zo</sound>mbie.

憾.meaning: A dog chews up his owner's favourite slipper, then sees her face. His <part>heartbeat</part> races and a great wave of <part>emotion</part> rolls over him. He drags in his best ball and drops it at her feet as an apology. Pure <kanji>remorse</kanji>.
憾.on: He even digs up a pink <sound>carn</sound>ation from the flowerbed for her.
憾.kun: She sighs '<sound>Oo</sound>h' and stays cross a whole minute, until he <sound>ru</sound>bs her ankles: to bear a grudge.

瞭.meaning: Lost in thick fog on a hill, a hiker squints until his <part>eye</part> waters. Then someone lights a <part>bonfire</part> on the peak, and the fog burns off in a ring around it: every path, sheep and signpost suddenly sharp. Now it's all <kanji>clear</kanji>.
瞭.on: Down the valley he spots the lanterns of a cosy <sound>ryo</sound>kan.
瞭.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' he cries, and finds the inn's <sound>key</sound> under a <sound>ru</sound>g by a <sound>cu</sound>p of tea.

嚇.meaning: A tiny lizard on a garden wall opens its <part>mouth</part> wide and flashes a bright <part>red</part> throat at the cat. It hisses. It's the size of a pencil, but the cat backs away very slowly. Small, but very <kanji>menacing</kanji>.
嚇.on: Afterwards it sits on a beetle <sound>carc</sound>ass like a king on his throne.
嚇.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps the cat, as it starts hissing at the <sound>do</sound>g next door too.

泰.meaning: After the holiday rush, the shoppers go home and the town square empties. The <part>Christmas tree</part> twinkles alone beside the <part>fountain</part>, which gurgles softly to itself, and a pigeon dozes on the rim. Everything is <kanji>peaceful</kanji>.
泰.on: The pigeon even wears a little bow <sound>tie</sound> for the occasion.

摯.meaning: A <part>tenacious</part> terrier spends all day digging up the park, ignoring every whistle. At dusk he trots home and drops one muddy treasure into his owner's <part>hand</part>: her lost wedding ring. Not a mess after all: a <kanji>gift</kanji>.
摯.on: She pins a medal shaped like a little <sound>shi</sound>eld on his collar.
摯.kun: <sound>Ea</sound>ger for a bath, he races her to the <sound>tu</sound>b and gets there first: to arrive.

擬.meaning: The crew hears the captain shout 'Drop the <part>anchor</part>!' and drops it. Then the captain storms on deck, full of <part>doubt</part>: 'I never said that.' Up on the mast, a cockatoo clears its throat and says it again in his exact voice. A perfect <kanji>mimic</kanji>.
擬.on: Next it copies the creak of the winch's rusty <sound>gea</sound>r.
擬.kun: The cook tries to hush it with a <sound>mu</sound>g of <sound>ga</sound>rlic soup, and it thanks him in his own voice: a fake.

浦.meaning: A giant on holiday swings his <part>flyswatter</part> at a fly on the beach. He misses and smacks a round dent in the coast. <part>Water drops</part> fly everywhere, the sea rushes in, and now the fishing boats have a calm little <kanji>bay</kanji> to shelter in.
浦.on: The fly lands on his <sound>ho</sound>tdog to celebrate.

勃.meaning: A <part>child</part> lies snoring under a <part>blanket</part> on the sofa. The clock strikes <part>ten</part>, the ice cream van chimes outside, and with one burst of <part>muscle</part> she's off the sofa and out the door, the blanket still flying behind her. Such <kanji>suddenness</kanji>.
勃.on: The wind of her dash knocks a row of toy ro<sound>bots</sound> off the shelf.
勃.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' gasps her dad, spilling his <sound>co</sound>ffee: things happen fast.

琴.meaning: A <part>king</part> can't sleep and wants music <part>now</part>. There's no band, so the cook strings fishing line across the bed frame and plucks it. The king dozes off at once, and the bed becomes his favourite instrument: the royal <kanji>harp</kanji>.
琴.on: A <sound>kin</sound>gfisher flies in through the window and lands on the strings with a twang.
琴.kun: As a reward, the cook gets a <sound>co</sound>ttage and a jar of <sound>to</sound>ffee.

脊.meaning: On a windy walk under the <part>moon</part>, a man's <part>umbrella</part> flips inside out and snaps <part>two</part> of its ribs. Only the straight shaft down the middle holds it together. He pats it fondly: what a strong <kanji>spine</kanji>.
脊.on: The torn cloth flaps like a pie chart with one <sound>sec</sound>tor missing.
脊.kun: He slides it down the back of his coat, gets <sound>se</sound>t, and marches home stiff as a post: the back.

鎌.meaning: A show-off farmer gets a curved <part>gold</part> blade for his birthday. He swings it and cuts the wheat while, <part>concurrently</part>, trimming his hedge and his own moustache. The field is a mess, but he loves his <kanji>sickle</kanji>.
鎌.on: A <sound>wren</sound> darts off with the moustache hairs for her nest.
鎌.kun: His <sound>ca</sound>lm old <sound>ma</sound>ma takes it off him and hangs it on a high hook.

劾.meaning: An <part>acrobat</part> keeps stopping mid-act to show off his <part>muscle</part>, flexing on the trapeze while his partner hangs there waiting. After the show the whole circus votes to tell him off in writing, stamped and signed. A formal <kanji>censure</kanji>.
劾.on: Even the ringmaster's <sound>gui</sound>de dog signs it with a paw.

捻.meaning: A bored sailor on the dock spins the <part>anchor</part> rope round and round his finger, making a <part>wish</part> with every spin: sun, fish, a pie. On the hundredth <kanji>twirl</kanji>, the rope flies loose and lassoes a passing pie cart.
捻.on: He tucks a crisp li<sound>nen</sound> napkin into his collar.
捻.kun: <sound>He</sound> twists his <sound>ne</sound>ck to watch the pie man chase his cart.

遵.meaning: At the skatepark, a <part>revered</part> old skater has painted the rules at the top of the <part>ramp</part>: helmets on, one at a time, no pushing. The kids grumble, then buckle up their helmets. Everyone at the park has to <kanji>abide by</kanji> them.
遵.on: Anyone who breaks a rule sits out under the <sound>jun</sound>iper bush for five minutes.

翁.meaning: Every morning a man with a long white beard sits on the same bench in the <part>public</part> park. The pigeons trust him so much they nest in his beard, and by noon he wears a coat of <part>feathers</part>. Nobody knows his age; they just call him the <kanji>old man</kanji> of the park.
翁.on: His bench sits in the shade of a huge <sound>oa</sound>k.
翁.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>, a <sound>key</sound>!' he says, pulling something from his beard. Then he looks again: '<sound>Nah</sound>, a twig.'

膳.meaning: Under the <part>moon</part>, a <part>virtuous</part> hedgehog sets out a little wooden board for the hungry fox next door: one bowl of rice, one of soup, and two chopsticks laid side by side. The fox can't believe it. Dinner, served on a <kanji>meal tray</kanji>.
膳.on: They eat it together beside a raked <sound>zen</sound> garden.
膳.kun: The fox licks the <sound>cu</sound>p clean, and then <sound>she</sound> <sound>wa</sound>nders home full.

緻.meaning: A tailor stitches a whole city map onto a postage stamp with one silk <part>thread</part>, every street and lamp in place. She uses it to <part>send</part> a letter to her brother, and the postman squints at it for an hour. Such <kanji>fine</kanji> work.
緻.on: A <sound>chee</sound>tah delivers it in four seconds flat.
緻.kun: Her brother pins it over his <sound>co</sound>t, next to his <sound>ma</sound>ma's tea <sound>cu</sound>p collection.

毀.meaning: A mole tunnels up under the mound of <part>soil</part> where a <part>maiden</part> keeps her heavy stone <part>mortar</part>. The mound tips, the mortar rolls down the steps and cracks clean in two. The mole peeks out, then ducks back in. Even stone can <kanji>break</kanji>.
毀.on: She glues it back together and locks the pieces in a box with a big brass <sound>key</sound>.
毀.kun: The crumbs she sweeps into her <sound>co</sound>ffee tin and buries under the <sound>bo</sound>nsai.

丙.meaning: An old train has <part>one</part> long roof over three kinds of seat. First class gets velvet, second gets cushions, and squeezed <part>inside</part> the very last car, people sit on crates beside the goats. That's the <kanji>third class</kanji> carriage.
丙.on: The goats munch the <sound>hay</sound> the seats are stuffed with.
丙.kun: '<sound>He</sound> <sound>no</sound>dded off on an <sound>e</sound>gg crate,' the guard says of one passenger.

准.meaning: A <part>sparrow</part> skates every day on a frozen pond with the swans' club, gliding on two chips of <part>ice</part> instead of skates. The swans won't make it a full member, so they pin a half badge on its chest. It's an <kanji>associate</kanji>.
准.on: It practises its spins round a frosty <sound>jun</sound>iper bush.

呉.meaning: At a street fair, a giant puppet head with a wide-open <part>mouth</part> waddles about on <part>eight</part> wobbly legs. Children drop sweets into the mouth, and it spits out a balloon for each. Swap a sweet, get a balloon: it loves to <kanji>give</kanji>.
呉.on: It even hands out swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles on hot days.
呉.kun: The fair's <sound>coo</sound>k gets a whole bunch of balloons and floats away waving.
